medicaid_program_name: Florida Medicaid (Statewide Medicaid Managed Care), administered by the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA). Eligibility for families, parents and caretaker relatives is decided by the Florida Department of Children and Families (DCF) through ACCESS Florida, and by the Social Security Administration for SSI recipients.
medicaid_adult_income_limit_note: DCF 'Medicaid Income Limits (Effective April 2026 – March 2027)' table, column 'Ages 19 & 20 and Parents and Caregivers' (monthly maximum income by household size): 1 = $356, 2 = $478, 3 = $600, 4 = $723. MACPAC (Feb 2026, levels as of July 2025) lists Florida parents and caretaker relatives at 22% FPL, with no coverage for other adults age 19-64 except 'Age 19–20 only'. DCF's Medicaid page lists the adult groups it covers as parents and caretaker relatives of children, pregnant women, former foster youth under 26, non-citizen emergencies, and aged or disabled people; it lists no group for other adults. Work requirement: no Florida Medicaid work requirement for 2027 was found. The federal H.R. 1 requirement applies to expansion adults, and Florida has none. KFF (secondary) reports that a 2026 Florida bill (SB 1758) to add work requirements passed the Senate but failed in the House.
medicaid_quote: Parents and other caretaker relatives of children up to age 18 who live with them may be eligible for Medicaid if the family’s countable income does not exceed certain income limits.

notes_unverified: Florida's non-expansion status comes from KFF (secondary, Nov 6, 2026) and MACPAC's Feb 2026 table (a federal agency compiling CMS data, treated as secondary). No Florida state page says 'not expanded' in those words. DCF's Medicaid page simply lists no group for other adults. Medicaid.gov's Florida state profile could not be read reliably: curl got 403, and WebFetch returned only template text that wrongly read 'has expanded coverage', so it was not used.

The DCF table header shown is 'Ages 19 & 20 and Parents and Caregivers'. The figures are monthly maximum countable income for the household size; for a parent, the household size includes the children. The table does not state a %FPL. MACPAC gives 22% FPL as of July 2025.
No Florida state premium subsidy or Section 1332 reinsurance program for 2027 was found: no Florida entry on CMS's 1332 page, and none on OIR's federal health insurance page. state_help is null.

Insurance regulator: OIR (floir.gov) regulates insurers and reviews health rates, and the Department of Financial Services (myfloridacfo.com) licenses agents. footprint.py uses DFS. Which to show depends on the link's role: aca_gen's resource line says 'insurance regulator, including agent license lookup', which covers both.

HealthCare.gov's dates page lists the dates without years under an 'Enroll for 2027 now' banner. The CMS fact sheet (Oct 30, 2026) gives the full 2027 dates. A 2025 CMS rule would have moved federal open enrollment to end Dec 15 starting with plan year 2027, but both CMS and HealthCare.gov currently show Jan 15, 2027, so Jan 15 is used.

A web-search summary said HealthCare.gov notes that, starting January 1, 2027, only people with certain immigration statuses qualify for Marketplace savings. This was not on the HealthCare.gov pages fetched, so it is not verified and not used in copy.

Checker: the Medicaid.gov primary table is dated Dec 1, 2023. Current status (not expanded) rests on that table plus KFF (secondary, Nov 6, 2026) and the DCF Medicaid page, which lists no group for adults without children. No newer CMS or Florida page saying 'not expanded' in those words was found.
